references.text: The parallel account in [ref:Matt 26:47-50|Matthew 26:47-50] gives the most detailed description of Judas's arrival with the crowd and the kiss as a sign of betrayal. Matthew includes Jesus's words to Judas: "Friend, do what you came for."

The parallel account in [ref:Mark 14:43-46|Mark 14:43-46] describes the same event where Judas arrives with a large crowd sent by the chief priests, the scribes and the elders, using the agreed-upon kiss to identify Jesus.

John's parallel account in [ref:Joh 18:2-5|John 18:2-5] tells of the same arrest, but without the kiss. John highlights that Judas came with a group of soldiers and temple guards, and that Jesus himself stepped forward and identified himself.
[ref:Luk 22:3-6|Luke 22:3-6] tells of Satan's entry into Judas and his agreement with the chief priests and leaders of the temple guard to betray Jesus. Verse 47 is the fulfillment of this betrayal.
[ref:Matt 26:14-16|Matthew 26:14-16] describes Judas's agreement with the chief priests to hand over Jesus for thirty silver coins. The event in Luke 22:47 is the execution of this plan.

[ref:Sal 41:10|Psalm 41:10] prophesies: "Even my close friend, someone I trusted, one who shared my bread, has turned against me." Judas, one of the twelve who ate with Jesus, fulfills this prophecy through his betrayal with a kiss.

[ref:Ordsp 27:6|Proverbs 27:6] says: "Wounds from a friend can be trusted, but an enemy multiplies kisses." Judas's kiss is the ultimate example of a deceitful kiss that hides hostility behind apparent devotion.

[ref:2 Sam 20:9-10|2 Samuel 20:9-10] tells of Joab approaching Amasa with apparent friendliness, kissing him, and then stabbing him with his sword. This is an Old Testament parallel to Judas's treacherous kiss.

[ref:Luk 6:16|Luke 6:16] mentions Judas Iscariot among the twelve apostles and identifies him as the one who became a traitor. In Luke 22:47 he is described as "one of the twelve", which underscores the tragedy of the betrayal.
[ref:Apg 1:16-18|Acts 1:16-18] is Peter's reflection on Judas's betrayal, where he confirms that Judas became a guide for those who arrested Jesus, directly pointing back to the event in Luke 22:47.
